claims.claimText: Under Code II.E and II.G, completed Accepting Responsibility creates an internal Academic Integrity Registry record despite not being a finding of guilt. Central records also include Primary Hearing/appeal guilt findings, course, charge, evidence summary, faculty decision, penalties and appeal outcome. Records must be disclosed to Hearing Boards considering other penalties for the same student and to college deans/associate deans for legitimate educational interests; other violation disclosures require student direction or law. A Board or Dean finding of no violation requires expunging all case records from the central registry and college files. No fixed retention duration is specified in II.G.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: The Accepting Responsibility process does not result in a finding of guilt under the Code of Academic Integrity. In that sense, the process is akin to a warning. But the process does provide for consequences in the form of a limited penalty and mandatory completion of a workshop.

academic_integrity.en: The Code explicitly covers unauthorized AI and fabricated citations. Findings require clear and convincing evidence; notice, response and review stages apply. Accepting Responsibility is voluntary and waives ordinary appeals. CTI discourages unreliable detectors; no detector score or AI use alone establishes guilt or an automatic sanction. Announced in-person Ithaca/Tech implementation scope and internal Registry records, disclosure limits and no-violation expungement must also be checked.
academic_integrity.zh: 守则明确涵盖未授权 AI 和虚假引用；认定须有清楚且令人信服的证据，并有通知、答复与复核程序。自愿 Accepting Responsibility 会放弃通常申诉。CTI 不推荐不可靠检测器，AI 使用或分数本身不自动定罪处分。 自愿承担责任的 Ithaca／Cornell Tech 线下课程实施范围、内部记录及披露／清除条件须另行核对。

teaching_guidance.en: Communicate course and assignment AI rules clearly. Instructors choose the permitted scope. The 2023 committee does not recommend AI summative grading; this is guidance, not a universal disciplinary prohibition.
